findings.issue_text: themes messages_en.properties (account-ui and admin-ui): error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from {{0}}-style placeholders to Java MessageFormat choice syntax {2,choice,...}; JS UIs (React/i18next) use {{n}} mustache interpolation and don't evaluate MessageFormat choice, so the literal {2,choice,...} string could be rendered to end users. Verify which formatting layer renders this key before switching syntax.

VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml: normalizeValue applies StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 to the raw translation before sanitization, so translations legitimately containing escaped entities (e.g. <b> as literal text) become actual HTML and are falsely reported as Illegal HTML, blocking valid translations.

VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors: value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(...)) removes the first occurrence of the anchor text anywhere in the string, which may not be the matched anchor (e.g. if the anchor text appears earlier as plain text). Should delete by match region, not by string content.

VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors: only anchors present in the translation but not in the English source are reported; extra/missing anchors relative to English are not validated when the translation has fewer, so a translation dropping a required link passes silently.

VerifyMessageProperties.containsHtml: HTML_TAGS regex <[a-z]+[^>]*> misses uppercase/mixed-case tags (e.g. <B>, <A HREF=...>); such tags won't enable HTML policy, and <A> isn't matched by ANCHOR_PATTERN either, so uppercase anchors slip through or cause false failures.

VerifyMessageProperties: the sanitizer normalizes tag syntax (e.g.
→
) and the verifier enforces byte-equality with sanitized output, forcing cosmetic-only rewrites across dozens of locale files and rejecting previously valid files for formatting rather than safety.

VerifyMessageProperties: RuntimeException thrown for IO errors instead of using the existing MojoExecutionException/messages reporting channel used by verify(); also the English-file path derived via replaceAll string surgery on the filename will fail/mis-resolve for files whose locale part or directory layout doesn't match assumptions, crashing the build rather than reporting a message.

misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml: owasp-java-html-sanitizer and commons-text versions are hard-coded rather than managed through Keycloak's parent/dependencyManagement (commons-text especially given its CVE history); pinned 20240325.1/1.13.0 will drift from the rest of the project and won't pick up dependency-management CVE bumps.

VerifyMessagePropertiesTest: no tests cover the normalizeValue special cases (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, choice-format keys, email RTL style stripping) or the anchor-stripping success path; also no test that a missing English key (fallback to "" → POLICY_NO_HTML) behaves as intended.

VerifyMessageProperties: the diff-stripping logic computing start/end assumes the difference is a contiguous middle region; when sanitization changes only a prefix or strings differ in length, sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) can produce an empty/misleading fragment in the error message rather than the actual offending HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: themes messages_en.properties (account-ui and admin-ui): error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from {{0}}-style placeholders to Java MessageFormat choice syntax {2,choice,...}; JS UIs (React/i18next) use {{n}} mustache interpolation and don't evaluate MessageFormat choice, so the literal {2,choice,...} string could be rendered to end users. Verify which formatting layer renders this key before switching syntax.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in `js/apps/*/messages_en.properties` from `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` placeholders to `{0}` plus Java `MessageFormat` choice syntax (`{2,choice,...}`), e.g. in `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties` and `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties`. The diff does not show what formatting/interpolation engine the JS UIs use, so it’s not verifiable from the diff alone that `{2,choice,...}` will be evaluated rather than rendered literally. However, the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded compatibility concern that should be checked before switching syntax in JS-delivered message bundles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml: normalizeValue applies StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 to the raw translation before sanitization, so translations legitimately containing escaped entities (e.g. <b> as literal text) become actual HTML and are falsely reported as Illegal HTML, blocking valid translations.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), normalizeValue() unconditionally applies StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value) to the raw bundle value before sanitization. That means a translation containing escaped markup intended as literal text (e.g., "<b>") is converted into real "<b>" prior to applying POLICY_NO_HTML / POLICY_SOME_HTML, so the sanitizer can strip/alter it and the subsequent comparison (sanitized vs. value) will report "Illegal HTML" even though the original file did not contain actual HTML tags. This can falsely fail verification and block valid translations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors: value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(...)) removes the first occurrence of the anchor text anywhere in the string, which may not be the matched anchor (e.g. if the anchor text appears earlier as plain text). Should delete by match region, not by string content.

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, `replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` removes the first occurrence of the *exact anchor tag string* (e.g., `` or ``). Since `matcher.find()` iterates through actual anchor tags (`]*>`), any earlier identical substring would also itself be an anchor tag and would have been matched in-order. The diff does not show a case where the same anchor-tag text appears earlier as non-anchor “plain text” yet would be removed incorrectly; with `Pattern.quote`, only the literal tag would match. So the claimed mis-removal is not verifiably a defect from the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors: only anchors present in the translation but not in the English source are reported; extra/missing anchors relative to English are not validated when the translation has fewer, so a translation dropping a required link passes silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, the loop only iterates over anchor tags found in the translation (`matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)`). If a translation contains fewer/no `<a>` tags than the English source, the method performs no checks and returns without reporting anything. There is also no post-check to ensure all anchors present in `englishValue` are also present in `value`. This makes the anchor validation one-sided (detects extra/modified anchors in translations, but not missing ones), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: VerifyMessageProperties.containsHtml: HTML_TAGS regex <[a-z]+[^>]*> misses uppercase/mixed-case tags (e.g. <B>, <A HREF=...>); such tags won't enable HTML policy, and <A> isn't matched by ANCHOR_PATTERN either, so uppercase anchors slip through or cause false failures.

adjudication.rationale:
In the newly added VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), containsHtml() uses `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which only matches lowercase tag names. Since HTML is case-insensitive, English source strings containing uppercase/mixed-case tags (e.g. ``, `
`, ``) would not be detected as “contains HTML”, causing `POLICY_NO_HTML` to be applied and potentially producing incorrect “Illegal HTML” reports. Similarly, `ANCHOR_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("]*>")` won’t match ``/``, so identical uppercase anchors in source/translation won’t be stripped by `santizeAnchors()` and will likely be flagged as illegal HTML (false failure) instead of being permitted when identical to the source.

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the code sanitizes each message value and then flags it as illegal whenever `!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)`. This means any canonicalization performed by the OWASP sanitizer (e.g., normalizing tag syntax) will be treated as “Illegal HTML” even if the original HTML was safe/allowed. The diff evidence supports this: many locale files were mechanically changed from `
` to `
`, consistent with a sanitizer normalization needed to satisfy byte-equality rather than safety. This is a false-positive behavior introduced by the strict equality check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: VerifyMessageProperties: RuntimeException thrown for IO errors instead of using the existing MojoExecutionException/messages reporting channel used by verify(); also the English-file path derived via replaceAll string surgery on the filename will fail/mis-resolve for files whose locale part or directory layout doesn't match assumptions, crashing the build rather than reporting a message.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), IO errors are wrapped in MojoExecutionException, but the newly added verifySafeHtml() reads bundles via FileInputStream and on IOException throws RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."), bypassing the existing MojoExecutionException/messages reporting path and potentially crashing the build. Additionally, the English properties path is derived via absolute-path replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties"); if the file layout/locale suffix doesn’t match these assumptions, it will try to open a non-existent file and throw RuntimeException rather than reporting a verifier message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml: owasp-java-html-sanitizer and commons-text versions are hard-coded rather than managed through Keycloak's parent/dependencyManagement (commons-text especially given its CVE history); pinned 20240325.1/1.13.0 will drift from the rest of the project and won't pick up dependency-management CVE bumps.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two new dependencies added in misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml with explicit <version> tags (owasp-java-html-sanitizer 20240325.1 and commons-text 1.13.0). That is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/governance concern because these versions are now pinned locally in this module rather than being centrally managed (e.g., via a parent/dependencyManagement), which can cause drift from the rest of the build and require manual updates for security/compat bumps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: VerifyMessagePropertiesTest: no tests cover the normalizeValue special cases (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, choice-format keys, email RTL style stripping) or the anchor-stripping success path; also no test that a missing English key (fallback to "" → POLICY_NO_HTML) behaves as intended.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `VerifyMessageProperties` (`verifySafeHtml()`, `normalizeValue()`, and `santizeAnchors()`), but the new/updated tests in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` only cover: duplicate keys, detecting illegal HTML, rejecting HTML when English has none, and the *failure* case for changed anchors. There are no fixtures/tests that exercise `normalizeValue`’s explicit special cases (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, the `{n,choice,...}` replacement for `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` / `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, or the email `style="direction: rtl;"` stripping), nor a test for the anchor *success* path (where translation anchor tags exactly match English and should be allowed). Also, `getEnglishValue()` falls back to `""` on missing keys (driving `POLICY_NO_HTML`), and there is no test verifying that behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: VerifyMessageProperties: the diff-stripping logic computing start/end assumes the difference is a contiguous middle region; when sanitization changes only a prefix or strings differ in length, sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) can produce an empty/misleading fragment in the error message rather than the actual offending HTML.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the code tries to highlight the difference by stripping a common prefix/suffix (computing start/end) and then reporting value.substring(start, value.length()-end) vs sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length()-end). This approach is safe (bounds-checked) but it can produce an empty fragment on one side (e.g., pure insertion/deletion) or a large/misleading middle segment when sanitization changes multiple disjoint parts, so the error message may not precisely show the offending HTML even though detection still works.
